A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Weight Space Consolidation study, despite retitling and substantial expansion. Their complete texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying changes.

before.justification: V2 reports original CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 experiments, including accuracy, training time, forgetting, component ablations, reset sensitivity and convergence analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original vision experiments and adds TRACE continual instruction-tuning results, plasticity measurements and further reset ablations.

M1.justification: The reset-and-average procedure remains, but parameter selection changes from absolute weight drift in v2 to the product of first- and second-gradient-moment statistics in v3 Equation 4. This is a localized algorithmic revision: retaining 20% of parameters, softly resetting the remainder and subsequently averaging weights are retained.

E1.justification: V3 retains CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 and adds continual instruction tuning across eight TRACE datasets: C-STANCE, FOMC, MeetingBank, Py150, ScienceQA, NumGLUE-cm, NumGLUE-ds and 20Minuten. This substantially extends coverage into language classification, summarization, code generation, mathematical reasoning and text simplification.

E2.justification: V3 retains the six vision comparators and adds MEMO. Its new TRACE comparison evaluates fine-tuning, Replay, SLERP, online and offline averaging, Task Arithmetic and MagMax (Table 7). V2 cited some merging methods but did not evaluate this comparator family.

E3.justification: The new TRACE protocol introduces LLaMA-3.2-1B, 20–80% replay fractions, one replay epoch, tuning at 20% memory with transfer to other fractions, task-specific metrics and VRAM-weighted runtime. Existing vision splits and backbones remain. CIFAR-to-ImageNet hyperparameter transfer is newly documented; v2 does not establish whether that practice changed.

E4.justification: The component ablation, retain-rate sweep and joint-versus-continual convergence study are retained; v2 Figure 5 becomes v3 Figure 2b. V3 newly reports plasticity-versus-memory curves and comparisons of importance metrics, random/reversion/soft resets, and reset frequency (Figure 7 and Tables 3–4), substantially expanding diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state five seeds for vision experiments. V3 adds explicit plus/minus uncertainty values to Tables 1, 5 and 6, whereas v2 tables report point estimates. The uncertainty statistic is not identified, and no increase in runs or uncertainty reporting for TRACE is established.

E6.justification: V3 adds TRACE, MEMO, plasticity and reset-analysis results and revises existing vision values. At 200 CIFAR exemplars, Replay changes from 70.84 to 71.60 and Ours from 73.48 to 74.49; at 100 exemplars, Ours changes from 68.41 to 67.25 (v2 Table 1; v3 Table 5). These are revised reports, with the proposed reset selector also changed.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix A.1.1 adds a local strong-convexity assumption and an explicit minimizer-distance bound to v2's informal proximity argument. Appendix A.1.2 adds gradient-alignment definitions and a derivation claiming vanishing updates as replay dominates (Equations 10–13). These are substantive formal additions, although alignment alone does not justify the claimed limit.

C1.justification: V3 extends the main contribution from image class-incremental learning to continual instruction tuning and elevates sufficient-memory plasticity loss into a central abstract/introduction claim. The general memory-versus-computation thesis and claimed three-to-fourfold cost reduction retain their earlier meaning, but their asserted application scope broadens substantially.

C2.justification: Reset's explanation shifts from maintaining proximity to a previous-task minimizer toward escaping its basin to recover plasticity. V3 develops replay-driven node-reuse interpretations and discusses offline merging failures. Section 6 also newly identifies privacy-sensitive or streaming-only environments and clean task boundaries as applicability limitations.

D1.justification: V3 substantially extends reproducibility documentation with TRACE framework use, LLaMA-3.2-1B, three V100 GPUs, one replay epoch and averaging every 20 iterations. It also documents hyperparameter transfer policies and adds library/dataset licensing information in Appendix A.8. The earlier vision hardware, PyTorch version and principal hyperparameters remain.

R1.justification: V3 broadens research positioning through continual language-model learning, model merging, pruning, gradient alignment and realistic hyperparameter selection, including Dziadzio et al. and Cha and Cho. Section 2 newly argues that some post-hoc merging approaches may violate sequential CL constraints, extending v2's emphasis on checkpoint-storage overhead.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of the method and experimental narrative are rewritten. Problem formulation becomes an expanded Motivation section, material moves from the appendix into the main argument, and separate reset, averaging, settings, results and ablation subsections create a substantially different exposition.

P2.justification: V3 moves memory-size line plots into the appendix, introduces accuracy–cost scatter panels, restructures benchmark tables and adds TRACE, plasticity and reset-strategy displays. Existing reset and convergence plots are relocated. A new presentation error occurs in Figure 11: its ImageNet-100 caption accompanies the exact CIFAR-100 graphic used in Figure 1.

improvement.justification: TRACE, MEMO, targeted ablations, uncertainty values and explicit limitations address v2's limited validation. However, v3's new central plasticity derivation does not justify vanishing updates from gradient alignment. Reporting also becomes less consistent: Tables 2 and 5 give Ours 73.57 versus 74.49 at 200 CIFAR exemplars without explaining the difference, and Figure 11 mislabels duplicated CIFAR data as ImageNet. The substantial empirical additions and these new reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
